page: Microsoft Azure F16ams_v6 is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the Famsv6 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and SHA_NI.

This instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It does not include local storage, though it is premium storage capable, and does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core tests. Multi-core performance is average in stress-ng multi-core tests but registers as strong in Geekbench multi-core and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests. Text processing performance is highly competitive, scoring in the top 10% on Geekbench. Memory performance is also strong, with PassMark memory scores in the top 25%, while memory bandwidth and database operations fall within the average range. For small LLM inference tasks using a 135M model, the server achieves top 10% text generation speeds and top 25% prompt processing speeds, though performance drops to average for medium 7B models.

Given its high memory density of 8.0 GB per core and dedicated AMD EPYC CPU resources, the F16ams_v6 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The instance is suited for memory-intensive applications, text processing pipelines, small-scale language model inference, and database operations relying on external premium storage.
